doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: From Peoria to Moline and the parade that made him want drums
summary: The family moves through Peoria and Rock Island to Moline, where his father opens his own music store. At three he points at the drums in a parade and his father starts him at three and a half.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You were born in one place in Illinois. Then you moved to Peoria. Then you moved to Moline. Do you have any recollections of Peoria?

Yes. My dad worked for Bierly Brothers’ music store. He had not gotten his own music store yet. He just taught there. We were there for about five years. Then we moved to Rock Island and then Moline. Finally my dad got his own music store. When I was – I’m backing up – when I was three years old, that’s when my dad took me to a parade. When that drum section passed me by, I said, “That’s what I want to play.” My dad said my little finger pointed right at the drums. I was so definite that he started me at three-and-a-half years old.
